title: Capstone 2: Sentiment Analysis API with TF Serving 📡
description: Train a text model, export a SavedModel, and deploy a REST API for real‑time predictions.

slides.title: The Goal: Instant Sentiment 🚀
slides.content:
# Deploy a Model as a Web Service

You'll build a model that classifies movie reviews as positive or negative, then wrap it in a **TensorFlow Serving**‑compatible SavedModel and test it with a REST client.

We'll cover:
- Data pipeline with `TextLineDataset`.
- Text vectorisation and Embedding.
- LSTM model.
- Export with signature.
- Test via `curl` (conceptual).

slides.title: Load and Preprocess Text
slides.content: Assume you have a `reviews.txt` and `labels.txt`. We'll simulate with IMDB dataset for demonstration.
slides.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.layers import TextVectorization

# Load IMDB
(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = tf.keras.datasets.imdb.load_data(num_words=10000)

# Pad sequences
maxlen = 200
x_train = tf.keras.preprocessing.sequence.pad_sequences(x_train, maxlen=maxlen)
x_test = tf.keras.preprocessing.sequence.pad_sequences(x_test, maxlen=maxlen)

train_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_train, y_train)).batch(32).prefetch(1)
test_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_test, y_test)).batch(32).prefetch(1)

slides.title: Build the LSTM Model
slides.codeSnippet:
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Embedding(10000, 128, input_length=maxlen),
    tf.keras.layers.Bidirectional(tf.keras.layers.LSTM(64, dropout=0.2, recurrent_dropout=0.2)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=test_ds, epochs=5)

slides.title: Export for Serving
Inspect and Test Locally
slides.codeSnippet:
# Load SavedModel
loaded = tf.saved_model.load('sentiment_model/1/')
infer = loaded.signatures['serving_default']
sample_input = tf.constant([x_test[0]])
pred = infer(input_text=sample_input)
print(pred['output_0'].numpy())

slides.title: Deploy with Docker & TF Serving
slides.content:
# Run the Server

```bash
docker run -p 8501:8501 \
  -v "$PWD/sentiment_model:/models/sentiment" \
  -e MODEL_NAME=sentiment \
  tensorflow/serving
```

Then send a request:
```bash
curl -d '{"instances": [[1,2,3,...,200]]}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  http://localhost:8501/v1/models/sentiment:predict
```

Your model is now a live API!

slides.title: Go Live 🛠️
slides.content: If you have Docker, run the server and send a real request. Observe the latency and response format.
